Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks — attached are the items we discussed. Deliverables in this message:

1) SOC2-summary-2026Q3.pdf — one-page summary (Type II, period: 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30). Full attestation available under NDA; summary includes scope and auditor.
2) redwood_filled_vendor_questionnaire.pdf — our responses to the CoralCare questionnaire (we answered all standard sections; flagged three items that will need artifact follow-up).
3) IR-playbook-excerpt.txt — short excerpt showing detection -> triage -> customer notification flow.
4) BCP-RTO-table.csv — hosted vs private deployment RTO/RPO guidance.

Key points called out from the questionnaire & playbook:
- HIPAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workloads. We offer a standard BAA; legal can start a review if you send your preferred template or we can init a Redwood BAA.
- GDPR / Data residency: We offer EU-region hosting (data at rest in EU) and can support subprocessor disclosures.
- Breach notification timelines: our standard approach is:
  - Initial detection alert: within 24 hours of confirmed detection to the named security contact.
  - Formal notification for confirmed incidents with customer impact: within 72 hours of confirmation (we accelerate if litigation or regulatory windows require faster notice).
  - Ongoing status updates: cadence agreed per incident (daily until containment, then weekly during remediation).
- BCP / DR: For hosted customers we provide an RTO target of 4–8 hours for critical inference endpoints (depends on model pinning and cache warm-up); private/on-prem deployments follow customer-managed runbooks and we provide runbook support and runbook templates.

Next steps I propose:
- Please confirm receipt and whether you want us to provide additional artifacts for the three flagged items in the questionnaire (we can share logs, config snaps, or redacted runbooks under an NDA).
- If CoralCare wants the BAA exchanged, loop your legal and I will get our legal counterpart aligned.
